title: Admin Settings Map
summary: Provides a full index of settings panels and what each control changes in system behavior.

warning.title: IMPORTANT
paragraphs: Administration settings directly change authorization, taxonomy, and workflow behavior. Run these changes with explicit change control and verification.

sections.title: Administration scope and access model
paragraphs: The administration workspace is a control plane for user access, platform taxonomy, template governance, and maintenance actions. It is exposed through `Settings` and section visibility is computed per session using role plus effective permissions.
A section can be hidden in the UI even when related APIs exist, so operational runbooks should treat the UI visibility model as the primary control boundary for administrators and managers.

sections.title: Section visibility matrix
paragraphs: Each settings panel has a distinct permission gate and operational data scope.

rows: Provision LDAP and local users, update role and optional permissions, delete accounts.
Rotate privileged admin password under policy checks.
Map IP addresses to source groups and synchronize matching records.
Control category taxonomy available for pentest finding classification.
Manage checklist definitions, auto-port mapping, enabled state, and canonical reset.
Manage PDF template catalog, template blocks, and enabled state for generation.
Run manual ingestion update and guarded pentest reset operations.

sections.title: Navigation and subsection behavior
paragraphs: The left settings drawer is stateful and supports subsection expansion for user workflows and report template selection. This keeps repeated admin flows on stable routes without forcing context switches.

User Management is split into three purpose-built subpages. Report Templates adds a `New Template` entry and a direct entry for each template, including disabled templates that are still manageable by authorized users.

rows: Use existing users for edits and deletion, LDAP for directory onboarding, local for non-directory accounts.
Use new template to create a template from defaults and template entries for targeted edits or reset.

sections.title: Recommended first-time setup sequence
paragraphs: A fixed setup sequence avoids hidden dependencies between permissions, taxonomy, and generated outputs.
orderedList: Create or verify user accounts and assign baseline roles.
Apply optional permissions only where needed for route or action access.
Configure IP Sources so imported records inherit meaningful source labels.
Review vulnerability categories before active testing starts.
Validate checklist and report templates, then enable only approved variants.
Run a manual update and a test report generation to confirm end-to-end behavior.

rows: Role defaults plus optional permission model
Role updates can hide sections and action buttons immediately after save.
Adding or deleting mapping updates matching records and sets `status` to `updated`.
New categories become available immediately for future finding entries.
Open ports parsing and checklist auto-enable logic
Template enablement and `auto_ports` can change checklist scope on pentest records.
Generated report pipeline and enabled template list
Template enabled state controls availability in report generation selector.

sections.title: Change verification and rollback pattern
paragraphs: After any administration change, verify both UI and API outcomes before closing the change. For sensitive updates, preserve before-and-after snapshots of affected entities.

Rollback should be explicit. Revert permissions by role and optional grants, restore template state using canonical reset for system templates, and reapply prior taxonomy values when operationally required.
